Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

# Kitty

Keeps track of shared trip costs and works out who owes whom. Needs only the
`python3` that comes with macOS (3.9 or newer). Data is kept in `kitty.json`
in whatever folder you run it from.

## Quick start

    python3 -m kitty init EUR
    python3 -m kitty member add Alice
    python3 -m kitty member add Bob
    python3 -m kitty expense add Alice 45 Dinner --category food
    python3 -m kitty balances
    python3 -m kitty settle

`python3 -m kitty --help` (or `python3 -m kitty expense add --help`) lists
every command and option.

## Behaviour worth knowing

- Outputs are JSON. Money is a two-decimal string, in the main currency except
  an expense's own `amount`. `expense add` prints just the new ID, and the
  other commands that change things print nothing.
- Errors go to stderr as `error: ...` and the exit status is 1.
- Splits are worked out to the cent and always add up to the full amount. When
  a cent can't be split evenly, it goes to whoever is listed first (for example
  10.00 split three ways comes out as 3.34 / 3.33 / 3.33).
- An expense in another currency is converted using the rate in effect when it
  is added. Changing the rate later doesn't change old expenses. `--exact`
  amounts are in the expense's own currency.
- The default "split between everyone" means everyone in the group when the
  expense is added. People who join later aren't added to old expenses.
- Expense IDs are never reused, even after an expense is removed.
- A member who is part of any expense or payment can't be removed, because
  that would make the totals stop adding up.
- `history` and the running totals are sorted by date, then by the order they
  were entered. Payments are worded from that
  person's side: "Payment to Alice" for the payer, "Payment from Bob" for
  the person paid back.
- Categories are stored in lowercase, so `Food` and `food` count as the same.
- Amounts can have at most two decimals. Descriptions with spaces work with or
  without quotes.

## Tests

    python3 -m unittest discover tests

- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

"""Tests for kitty. Run with: python3 -m unittest discover tests"""

import csv
import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest

PROJECT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))


class KittyTestCase(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.dir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        self.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, self.dir)

    def run_kitty(self, *args):
        env = dict(os.environ, PYTHONPATH=PROJECT)
        return subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "kitty"] + list(args), cwd=self.dir,
                              env=env, capture_output=True, text=True)

    def ok(self, *args):
        result = self.run_kitty(*args)
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        return result.stdout

    def json(self, *args):
        return json.loads(self.ok(*args))

    def fails(self, *args):
        result = self.run_kitty(*args)
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 1, result.stdout + result.stderr)
        self.assertIn("error:", result.stderr)
        self.assertNotIn("Traceback", result.stderr)
        return result.stderr

    def group(self, *names, currency="EUR"):
        self.ok("init", currency)
        for name in names:
            self.ok("member", "add", name)


class TestSamsExamples(KittyTestCase):
    def test_examples(self):
        self.group("Alice", "Bob")
        self.ok("rate", "set", "USD", "0.92")
        out = self.ok("expense", "add", "Alice", "45", "Dinner", "--currency", "USD",
                      "--date", "2026-07-14", "--category", "food")
        self.assertEqual(out.strip(), "1")
        self.assertEqual(self.json("member", "list"), ["Alice", "Bob"])
        self.assertEqual(self.json("expense", "list"), [{
            "id": 1, "date": "2026-07-14", "payer": "Alice", "description": "Dinner",
            "amount": "45.00", "currency": "USD", "base_amount": "41.40", "category": "food",
            "shares": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}}])
        self.assertEqual(self.json("balances"), {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "-20.70"})
        self.assertEqual(self.json("settle"), [{"from": "Bob", "to": "Alice", "amount": "20.70"}])
        self.assertEqual(self.json("history", "Bob"), [{
            "date": "2026-07-14", "description": "Dinner", "change": "-20.70",
            "balance": "-20.70"}])
        self.assertEqual(self.json("report"), {"food": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}})


class TestMembers(KittyTestCase):
    def test_add_remove(self):
        self.group("Alice", "Bob")
        self.ok("member", "remove", "Bob")
        self.assertEqual(self.json("member", "list"), ["Alice"])

    def test_cannot_remove_someone_with_expenses(self):
        self.group("Alice", "Bob")
        self.ok("expense", "add", "Alice", "10", "Taxi")
        self.assertIn("expense 1", self.fails("member", "remove", "Bob"))

    def test_errors(self):
        self.group("Alice")
        self.fails("member", "add", "Alice")
        self.fails("member", "remove", "Nobody")
        self.fails("member", "add", "A,B")


class TestSplits(KittyTestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        super().setUp()
        self.group("Alice", "Bob", "Carol")

    def shares(self):
        return self.json("expense", "list")[-1]["shares"]

    def test_equal_split_rounds_to_the_cent(self):
        self.ok("expense", "add", "Alice", "10", "Snacks")
        self.assertEqual(self.shares(), {"Alice": "3.34", "Bob": "3.33", "Carol": "3.33"})
        self.assertEqual(self.json("balances"),
                         {"Alice": "6.66", "Bob": "-3.33", "Carol": "-3.33"})

    def test_among(self):
        self.ok("expense", "add", "Alice", "30", "Museum", "--among", "Bob,Carol")
        self.assertEqual(self.shares(), {"Bob": "15.00", "Carol": "15.00"})

    def test_exact(self):
        self.ok("expense", "add", "Alice", "50", "Hotel", "--exact", "Alice=30,Bob=20")
        self.assertEqual(self.shares(), {"Alice": "30.00", "Bob": "20.00"})

    def test_shares(self):
        self.ok("expense", "add", "Alice", "30", "Fuel", "--shares", "Alice=2,Bob=1")
        self.assertEqual(self.shares(), {"Alice": "20.00", "Bob": "10.00"})

    def test_percent(self):
        self.ok("expense", "add", "Alice", "50", "Boat", "--percent", "Alice=60,Bob=40")
        self.assertEqual(self.shares(), {"Alice": "30.00", "Bob": "20.00"})

    def test_exact_in_foreign_currency_converts(self):
        self.ok("rate", "set", "USD", "0.9")
        self.ok("expense", "add", "Alice", "50", "Hotel", "--currency", "usd",
                "--exact", "Alice=30,Bob=20")
        expense = self.json("expense", "list")[-1]
        self.assertEqual(expense["currency"], "USD")
        self.assertEqual(expense["base_amount"], "45.00")
        self.assertEqual(expense["shares"], {"Alice": "27.00", "Bob": "18.00"})

    def test_split_errors(self):
        self.fails("expense", "add", "Alice", "50", "x", "--exact", "Alice=30,Bob=10")
        self.fails("expense", "add", "Alice", "50", "x", "--percent", "Alice=60,Bob=60")
        self.fails("expense", "add", "Alice", "50", "x", "--shares", "Alice=two")

I've added `expense edit ID` and `--in CUR` for `balances` and `settle`, and both work as you described. The 25 existing tests still pass, and 10 new ones for the two features pass too.

**`expense edit ID`**
- It changes only the options you give. The expense keeps its ID and its place in the order it was entered, even if you change its date.
- If the amount or currency changes and you give no split option, it's split equally among the same people as before. That's true even if it was first split with `--exact` or `--shares`.
- With a split option, the split is worked out against the new amount and currency.
- A new currency is converted at its current rate. Passing `--currency` with the currency it already has doesn't count as new.
- If any part of an edit is invalid, nothing is saved. That covers things like an unknown payer, a currency with no rate, `--exact` amounts that don't add up, or two split options at once.
- `expense edit 1` with no options is an error ("nothing to change"), not a silent no-op.

**`--in CUR`**
- Amounts are worked out in the base currency as usual, then converted at the current rate and rounded to the cent. The JSON looks the same as now.
- Because each amount is rounded on its own, the converted balances may not add up to exactly zero.
- A currency with no rate, or a badly written code, is an error. Using the base currency gives the usual output.

**One decision for you:** your spec doesn't say what rate to use when only the amount changes on a foreign-currency expense. I used the rate the expense was added with, because the README says changing a rate later doesn't change old expenses.
- Kitty never saved that rate, so new expenses now save it in `kitty.json` (as a `rate` field). It doesn't appear in `expense list` or the CSV export, and older files still load.
- For expenses added before this change, the rate is worked out from the saved amount and converted amount. That can be off by about a cent per edit.
- If you'd rather a changed amount use the current rate, that's a small change.

The code is in `kitty/core.py` and `kitty/cli.py`, and the README has a note on both features.
